title: Minimum Swaps to Arrange Binary Grid

monster.name: Matrix Rotator
monster.title: Bubbler of Upper-Triangular Rows
monster.defeatQuote: Minimum adjacent row swaps to form all-zero upper triangular matrix!

description: Given an `n x n` binary `grid`, in one step you can choose two adjacent rows of the grid and swap them. A grid is said to be valid if all the cells above the main diagonal are zeros. Return the minimum number of steps needed to make the grid valid, or -1 if impossible.
solutionCode:
def minSwaps(grid: list[list[int]]) -> int:
    n = len(grid)
    trailing_zeros = []
    for row in grid:
        count = 0
        for val in reversed(row):
            if val == 0: count += 1
            else: break
        trailing_zeros.append(count)
    swaps = 0
    for i in range(n):
        req = n - 1 - i
        found = -1
        for j in range(i, n):
            if trailing_zeros[j] >= req:
                found = j
                break
        if found == -1: return -1
        swaps += found - i
        val = trailing_zeros.pop(found)
        trailing_zeros.insert(i, val)
    return swaps
hints: Compute trailing zeroes per row. Row i requires >= n - 1 - i trailing zeroes. Greedily bubble the first qualifying row upwards.
